exercises.name: Easy Traversing Warm-Up
exercises.description: A gentle climbing warm-up that activates muscles and prepares the body for harder climbing.
howTo: Choose a low-angle section of the wall with large holds.
Traverse sideways for 2–3 minutes, staying on easy terrain.
Focus on smooth, controlled movement and good footwork.
Repeat on different wall angles to activate a variety of muscles.
exercises.info: Avoid rushing this warm-up. Gradually increase intensity as you feel your body warming up.

exercises.name: Dead Hangs
exercises.description: A finger strength exercise performed by hanging statically from a hangboard.
howTo: Warm up thoroughly before starting.
Grip a set of edges on the hangboard using both hands.
Hang for 7–10 seconds, keeping shoulders engaged.
Rest for 1–2 minutes between hangs and repeat for several sets.
exercises.info: Focus on shoulder engagement and avoid shrugging.

notification.msg: Do not attempt this exercise when exhausted or at the end of your session.

exercises.name: 4x4s
exercises.description: A high-intensity climbing drill designed to improve power endurance by simulating sustained effort.
howTo: Choose four boulder problems of moderate difficulty that you can complete when fresh.
Prefer slightly overhanging or vertical terrain to build endurance.
Climb the first problem, rest briefly, and move immediately to the next.
Complete all four problems, rest 2–4 minutes, then repeat three more times.
exercises.info: Maintain good technique even as fatigue builds.

notification.msg: Avoid this exercise when tired; it places high stress on fingers and forearms.

exercises.name: Lock-Off Holds
exercises.description: An upper-body strength exercise that builds control and stability during static moves.
howTo: Find a section of wall or system board with good holds.
Pull up until your arm forms a 90-degree angle and hold the position for 3–5 seconds.
Lower slowly and repeat on the other arm.
Perform 3–5 reps per side for several sets.
exercises.info: Engage your core to prevent swinging or shoulder strain.

exercises.name: Foot-On Fingerboard Repeaters
exercises.description: A finger endurance exercise performed on a hangboard with partial weight support from your feet.
howTo: Place your feet on a chair or footholds to reduce load.
Grip the edges and hang for 7 seconds, then rest for 3 seconds.
Repeat this hang/rest cycle 6 times per set.
Rest 2–3 minutes between sets.
exercises.info: Adjust foot support to control intensity.

notification.msg: Avoid doing this exercise when your fingers are sore or fatigued.

exercises.name: Core Tension Leg Raises
exercises.description: A core-strength exercise that improves body tension for overhangs and roof climbing.
howTo: Hang from a pull-up bar or jug holds.
Engage your core and lift your legs to hip height or higher.
Lower them slowly with control and repeat.
Perform 3 sets of 8–10 reps.
exercises.info: Keep your body still and avoid swinging.

exercises.name: Downclimbing Drills
exercises.description: A control and endurance exercise where you climb down routes to improve efficiency and technique.
howTo: Climb an easy problem or route to the top.
Downclimb using the same holds in reverse, maintaining slow and deliberate movements.
Focus on smooth foot placement and control.
Repeat 3–5 times.
exercises.info: Helps improve route reading and control under fatigue.

exercises.name: Tension Plank with Shoulder Taps
exercises.description: A core and shoulder stability exercise that enhances body control on the wall.
howTo: Start in a plank position with your body fully straight.
Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder while keeping your hips stable.
Alternate sides for 20–30 seconds per round.
Rest 30 seconds and repeat for 3–4 rounds.
exercises.info: Maintain tension through your core and avoid rotation.

exercises.name: ARC Training (Aerobic Restoration and Capillarity)
exercises.description: A low-intensity endurance exercise for building aerobic capacity in the forearms.
howTo: Climb continuously on easy terrain for 15–30 minutes without reaching failure.
Stay in a comfortable zone where you can maintain a conversation.
Focus on smooth, efficient movement and relaxed grip.
exercises.info: Excellent for base endurance during training cycles.

exercises.name: Yoga for Climbers Cool-Down
exercises.description: A cool-down session focused on flexibility, mobility, and recovery after climbing.
howTo: Include poses such as downward dog, pigeon pose, and shoulder stretches.
Hold each pose for 20–30 seconds, focusing on slow breathing.
Move gently and avoid forcing range of motion.
exercises.info: Promotes recovery and reduces muscle tension after training.
